tagline: Trat's mountainous island — far-eastern Gulf outpost, a roadmap node off the seaboard.
summary: Koh Chang is Thailand's second-largest island, a mountainous national-park destination in Trat province near the Cambodian border. It is reached today by car ferry from Laem Ngop. It sits well east of Pattaya (a long Gulf leg), so it features as a far-eastern Eastern-Seaboard outpost and longer-horizon node rather than a near-term short hop — its internal and mainland-gateway crossings are the near-term Pioneer II opportunities.

demand_signals.detail: Large protected island with steady leisure demand from Bangkok and the east.
Mainland access is via Laem Ngop car ferries — slow, with no premium passenger tier.
Distant from Pattaya; the mainland-gateway and intra-island legs are the near-term fits.

use_cases: Laem Ngop <-> Koh Chang gateway crossing

journeys.note: Short mainland-gateway crossing — the near-term fit.

navier_fit: Moderate near-term: the short Laem Ngop gateway and intra-archipelago hops are clean Pioneer II legs. The Pattaya link is a long Gulf leg held for the roadmap, not drawn near-term.
competitive_landscape: Car ferries from Laem Ngop; no premium passenger or in-app tier; intra-archipelago hops on small boats.
seasonality: Peak: Nov-Apr; the far-eastern Gulf is more exposed in the SW monsoon.
regulatory_note: Thai Marine Department licensing; Mu Ko Chang National Park rules; Trat provincial coordination.
signature_routes: Koh Chang <-> Koh Mak / Koh Kood

precedents.label: Laem Ngop ferry market
precedents.note: Existing mainland-gateway demand a premium tier can upgrade.

grab.super_app_fit: In-app Koh Chang gateway + intra-archipelago transfers (boat + GrabCar) from Trat.
grab.wedge: Far-eastern Eastern-Seaboard outpost: near-term value in the gateway and intra-island hops, not a Pattaya line.

transit_planning.note: Eastern Seaboard far-eastern outpost; long Pattaya leg held for roadmap. Brief deepened in depth pass.
